name: Armpit shaving

card.summary: Shaving the pits to cut odor-holding hair; the one study found shaved and unshaved smelled the same.
card.note: Razor irritation; shared barber equipment has been linked to hepatitis C transmission in Pakistan.

quick.overview:
Armpit shaving removes underarm hair with a razor. Some in grooming communities do it hoping to reduce odor, reasoning that hair holds sweat and bacteria.

The evidence is thin. A 2012 study cited on Wikipedia reported that shaved and unshaved armpits were rated as smelling the same.
quick.mechanism: A razor cuts the hair at the skin surface, and regrowth occurs within days. Odor itself comes from bacteria acting on apocrine sweat.
quick.risks: Reported risks include skin irritation, increased absorption of deodorant chemicals through damaged skin, and, with shared unsterilised barber tools, infection transmission.

lead: Armpit shaving is the removal of underarm hair at the skin surface with a razor. People do it for a cleaner, smoother look under raised arms and in sleeveless or fitted clothing, and for the belief that it helps them smell fresher. It is the most common form of hair removal, and its results last only hours to days. [1]

In looksmaxxing and grooming discussions it is proposed as a way to reduce body odor, on the reasoning that hair gives bacteria and sweat more surface to cling to. Body odor in the armpit arises mainly when skin bacteria such as Corynebacterium and Staphylococcus break down secretions from apocrine sweat glands. [2] One study cited on Wikipedia's underarm hair page reported that shaved and unshaved armpits were rated as smelling the same, and the function of underarm hair itself is described as unclear. [3] Published evidence on the topic is limited.

chain: Razor cuts underarm hair at the skin surface
Less hair for sweat and odor-producing bacteria to cling to (as practitioners reason)
Smoother underarm appearance and, practitioners say, less odor
angle.text: The look is immediate: bare, smooth underarms. The odor benefit is the claimed part. Some users report needing less deodorant after shaving, whereas the one study cited on Wikipedia found raters could not tell shaved from unshaved armpits by smell. [3][5]

paras: Shaving cuts hair at the skin surface rather than removing the follicle, so regrowth is quick. [1] Underarm hair removal by shaving or other methods is common in some cultures, particularly among women. [3] On T Nation, one member says he can handle shaving his armpits and the occasional lower leg but nothing beyond that, while another jokes about a poster being told to shave before posting on a bodybuilding forum. [6][7]

Razors and depilation go back to ancient Egypt, where pumice and razors were used, and the safety straight razor was invented in Paris in 1760 by Jean-Jacques Perret. [1] Women in Europe and America did not make hair removal routine until the late nineteenth century. In 1915 Harper's Bazaar ran the first women's fashion magazine campaign calling underarm hair removal a necessity, and Gillette soon launched the Milady Decollete, the first safety razor marketed to women, advertised as keeping the underarm white and smooth. [1]
Wikipedia also notes that competitive swimmers shave arms and torsos to reduce drag, and that footballers and road cyclists remove leg hair so injuries are easier to clean and treat. [1]

The importance of underarm hair is described as unclear. It may wick sweat away from the skin, aiding ventilation, and some claim it traps odor, a statement the page flags as needing a source. [3] Wikipedia's body odor article attributes armpit odor primarily to apocrine sweat gland secretions broken down by bacteria. Corynebacterium produces lipases that release molecules such as butyric acid, and Staphylococcus hominis produces thioalcohols. It describes armpit hair as springy and helping diffuse odors, without discussing shaving. [2]

Genetics also matter: a loss-of-function variant in the ABCC11 gene reduces apocrine odor precursors and is common in East Asians (80 to 95 percent) but rare in European and African populations. [2] Deodorants reduce odor, antiperspirants temporarily block sweat pores, and daily washing with antibacterial soap reduces skin bacteria. [2] A 2012 study cited on the underarm hair page found shaved armpits were rated the same for odor as unshaved ones. [3]

Wikipedia lists general hair removal problems including skin inflammation, minor burns, lesions, scarring, ingrown hairs, bumps and folliculitis. [1] A 2017 study cited on the underarm hair page reported that deodorant chemical absorption rose from about 0.01 percent to 0.06 percent where skin was damaged by recent shaving. A 2003 study tentatively linked underarm shaving combined with antiperspirant use to breast cancer, but later studies found no significant increase among users. [3]

In Pakistan, researchers have reported that many hepatitis C patients have a history of facial or armpit shaving at barber shops, and a 2011 laboratory study examined potash alum stones used on shaving cuts as a possible route of virus transmission. [4] This concerns shared, unsterilised barber equipment rather than personal razors.

No randomized trials of armpit shaving for body odor were found. A 2012 study cited on the underarm hair page reported that shaved and unshaved armpits were rated as smelling the same. [3] Research on barber-shop shaving and hepatitis C transmission is epidemiological or laboratory work and concerns infection risk, not odor. [4]

timeline.event: Jean-Jacques Perret invents the safety straight razor in Paris. [1]
Harper's Bazaar campaign presents underarm hair removal as a necessity for women; Gillette's women's razor follows. [1]
Study cited on Wikipedia finds shaved and unshaved armpits rated the same for odor. [3]

lore.intro: On T Nation, armpit shaving comes up in grooming and bodybuilding threads, sometimes with odor claims. [5][6]

claims.claim: Shaving the armpits means you can go much longer without deodorant
claims.believers: A poster says that since shaving his armpits he can go almost an entire day without deodorant without a hint of odor, though sweating from activity brings odor back. [5]
claims.experts: A 2012 study cited on Wikipedia found shaved and unshaved armpits rated the same for odor. [3] Wikipedia attributes odor mainly to bacterial breakdown of apocrine secretions. [2]

claims.believers: Grooming advice often says hair holds sweat and bacteria. [3]
claims.experts: Wikipedia's underarm hair article describes the function of the hair as unclear and notes the odor-trapping claim has no citation; the body odor article describes armpit hair as helping diffuse odors. [2][3]

claims.claim: Shaving irritates skin and may increase chemical absorption
claims.believers: Users cite razor irritation as a downside of shaving.
claims.experts: A 2017 study reported deodorant chemical absorption rose from 0.01 to 0.06 percent on recently shaved, damaged skin. [3]
